s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic facial swelling with reduced mouth opening and prior similar episodes
salient_findings: Asymptomatic swelling in the right lower half of the face
Ovoid subcutaneous swelling with ill-defined borders
Elevated and glistening right buccal mucosa
key_facts: 62-year-old man
Two-week history of facial swelling
Two prior similar episodes over eight years
No pain or fever
Known diabetic on regular medication
6 × 6 cm ovoid subcutaneous swelling
Swelling extended from the level of the right lateral canthus to 1 cm below the corner of the mouth
Restricted mouth opening due to the mass
Contrast-enhanced CT showed a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas
Intracystic loculations with dense cystic content
Erosion of the posterior buccal cortex without perforation of the maxilla
Maxillary antrum was compressed

shortlist.label: Buccal space abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical diagnosis and CT findings of a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas

shortlist.label: Dentigerous cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of facial swelling and restricted mouth opening

shortlist.label: Staphylococcal lymphadenitis
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of recurrent facial swelling episodes

shortlist.label: Sialadenitis
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of facial swelling and painless episodes

shortlist.label: Kimura disease
shortlist.why_kept: Rare but possible cause of chronic facial swelling and lymphadenopathy

raw.rationale: The presence of a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas and intracystic loculations with dense cystic content on contrast-enhanced CT, along with the history of recurrent similar episodes and the absence of pain or fever, suggests a mucocele, which is a type of benign cystic lesion that can cause swelling and is often associated with the buccal space.

rejected.label: Staphylococcal abscess
rejected.why: The absence of pain, fever, and lymphadenopathy, as well as the lack of a clear infectious history, makes a staphylococcal abscess less likely.
